results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 13 outline summaries state the controlling idea of the aligned spec paragraph, in the spec's order. Two summaries are thinner than the spec idea without contradicting it: the p05 summary gives the five questions and the build-on order but not the search exception; the p10 summary omits that the chapter solves the problem the search chapter leaves open.

Introduction ¶2 (p02), marked two_ideas by the outliner: ruled one idea. The paragraph opens on Part I's rule (one record per fact, every other value a copy) and applies both halves of it: the records become four owners, the other values become copies with a source and a comparison. Both of the outliner's summaries are the two halves of that one rule, which is also the part's single claim.

Chapters in this part ¶3 (p08), marked two_ideas by the outliner: ruled one idea, narrowly. The unit describes one chapter, and the gift-card sentence is a scope note of that chapter with its reason given ('which are money the merchant owes'); it belongs to the same supporting claim, P2-3. Residual weakness, not a failure: the sentence opens with 'also' and is not tied to the bolded question; saying why the separation matters for refunds would close it.

Every unit ties to the claim: p01 is its example, p02 and p02a state it, p03 places its four facts in the order, p04 names the cases it is tested on, p05 orders the questions; p06 to p10 introduce the chapters for P2-1 to P2-5, with P2-6 named in the pricing, search and inventory paragraphs; p11 and p12 conclude.

Each item is followed or accompanied by what it shows: the jacket example by 'Updating both on the same schedule can leave the page accurate about the product but wrong about whether it can be bought'; Figure 1 and Figure 2 by captions that say what they show; Eva's order by 'All of these facts are needed before "add to cart"'; the season entered four times by 'no version was the owner's, which motivates a PIM'; the €179 price by the three remedies that address it; the 2,860 orders by 'nobody owned how offers combine'; the waterproof jacket by 'correcting them improves ... search results without replacing the engine'; the oversell by 'shows the cost of delayed copies'.

Declared: additional_support, carrying over the claim about owners and copies and introducing its last step. The draft's 'One step remains' does not say what the step belongs to: the paragraph before it is not a sequence of steps, and nothing names the claim. Both flow readers stopped here (flow1: 'It was not clear what this is a step of; nothing before it was a sequence of steps'; flow2: '"Step" made me think of the order's thirteen steps, but it means a remaining part of the argument'). Fix: name the claim, e.g. 'The claim has one more part: once an order is placed, ...'.
results.quote: One step remains: once an order is placed, the price, the discount and the unit promised to it are fixed on that order

results.finding: All other boundaries express the declared relationship and pick up the declared known information: p02 ('Part I ended on a rule ... Part II applies it to the facts a shopper reads before buying'), p03 ('Where we are in the order's journey'; see the flow result on 'these facts'), p04 ('needs each of those facts to be right ... cases in which one of those facts was wrong'), p05 ('takes those disagreements as five questions in order'), the chapter section (the question list and the order rule at the end of p05), p07 ('then establishes, per variant'), p08 ('starts from the selected price'), p10 ('solves a problem the search chapter leaves open'), the conclusion ('Together, the five answers'), p12 ('the chapter for its fact'). Weakest of these: p09's contrast is carried only by 'the index owns none of it' and does not name the owned facts of the three chapters before it; p12's cause-effect has no marker. Neither stopped a reader.

Both flow readers lost the referent of 'these facts': the sentence before it (p02a) is about what happens after the order is placed, so the pointer has to reach back past it and Figure 2 to the four facts of p02. flow1: '"these facts" briefly seemed to point at the frozen values. I re-read both.' flow2: 'I had to look back two paragraphs to find "these facts".' Both name the position of p02a as the cause and give the same one reordering (move 'One step remains' to the end of the claim paragraph before Figure 2, or after Eva's paragraph / to the closing), so the difficulty comes from the declared order: an after-the-order statement stands between the four facts and the paragraph that places them before 'add to cart'. A prose-only repair exists and may be enough for the author: name the facts in p03 ('Content, price, discount and stock status are all needed before "add to cart"').
results.quote: All of these facts are needed before "add to cart".
results.corroborated_by: reader-flow2, item 3, second bullet ('I had to look back two paragraphs to find "these facts"') and item 4

results.finding: Both readers re-read the sentence: 'four' followed by 'the fourth' reads as if the fourth were one of the four. flow1: 'I had to count: the fourth of five is the exception, not one of the "four".' flow2: 'reads at first as a contradiction, until I worked out that the four are questions 1, 2, 3 and 5'. The order is fine; the wording hides it. Fix: say which questions, e.g. 'The fourth question concerns search, which owns none of the four facts; the other four take one fact each.'
results.quote: Four questions concern the four facts; the fourth concerns search.
results.corroborated_by: reader-flow2, item 3, fourth bullet ('I re-read this ... reads at first as a contradiction')

results.finding: Both readers could not tell what 'its' refers to. flow1: '"Its" has no clear owner (the chapter's? the fact's?)'. flow2: 'I could not tell whose copies "its" means: the chapter's, the fact's or Kestrel & Pine's.' Fix: name the owner, e.g. 'Each chapter starts with one disagreement between two of the company's copies of a fact.'
results.quote: Each chapter starts with one disagreement between its copies.
results.corroborated_by: reader-flow2, item 3, third bullet ('I could not tell whose copies "its" means')

results.finding: One reader only (flow1): 'I parsed "cannot shows" twice before it resolved. Search also arrives here with no introduction, as a fifth thing in a paragraph about four.' Not reported by flow2. Fix: 'A channel that cannot ask shows a copy', and give search a clause of its own.
results.quote: A channel that cannot shows a copy, and so does search, which owns none of the four facts.

results.finding: One reader only (flow1): the callout's second case is 'never named again in those words (I assume it is the Black Friday oversell)'. The chapter list calls it 'The Black Friday oversell of 1,340 jackets' and never mentions a marketplace or an empty shelf; the AC-2 reader also listed the two as separate cases. Not reported by flow2. The spec's decision log records that the callout wording is the author's and was kept. Fix: one name for the case in both places.
results.quote: The €179 German price and the marketplace selling an empty shelf were copies nobody compared with their source.

results.finding: 'allocated to every line' is used in the callout and nowhere explained. Discount allocation is on the audience's does_not_know list ('only named here'), and the body gives the same point in plain words ('how discounts reach invoices and refunds') without connecting them; 'line' (an order line) is not introduced on this page. A flow reader reported it: flow2, 'the key points say "the discount allocated to every line"; "allocated" and "line" are not explained on this page' (the reader rated it minor). Fix: plain words in the bullet, e.g. 'the discount is shared out over the items on the order'.
results.quote: the discount allocated to every line
results.corroborated_by: reader-flow2, item 3, sixth bullet ('"allocated" and "line" are not explained on this page')

results.finding: All other terms are known or given where first used: SKU and GTIN appear only in plain words ('internal stock codes and global barcode identifiers'); the search index is glossed in Figure 2's caption before the roadmap uses it; PIM is spelled out; commitments are glossed ('units already promised to orders'); dated prices appear as 'prices with a start date'; reconciliation is glossed in Figure 2's caption. Each paragraph opens from something already introduced, except the two openings reported under the transition and flow checks.
None of the weak patterns: the introduction opens on a specific example (one jacket page, two facts with different speeds), states the claim and gives a roadmap.

None of the weak patterns: it does not open with 'in conclusion', does not end on a rephrased thesis alone, adds no evidence and no new subtopic; it ends on a course of action and the hand-off to product-information.

States of the whole page what each chapter says of one fact (every fact an owner and a path to every channel; every copy, the search result included, a named source and a comparison), and gives the so-what: 'when a page or listing is wrong, ask first which fact is wrong and who owns it, and only then for faster synchronization'.
Returns to the element named in callback.to: 'the description, the price, the discount and the stock badge on the opening's product page', now seen as separate facts each with an owner.

The reader of the introduction alone named the five chapters in order and in the expected terms: who owns content and identifiers; who selects a price and how channels receive it; how discounts and offers combine and reach invoices and refunds; what feeds the search index, a copy that owns none of the facts; what 'in stock' means. For the fifth the reader gave 'what in stock means, and how the last unit is committed to exactly one order', not the expected physical stock against what a channel may still sell: the same subject, less exact. The reader also predicted the evidence (Kestrel & Pine cases, Eva's order, diagrams) and the tone.

The reader gave all three parts of the expected answer: the description may stay unchanged for a season while the last unit can go while the page is open; one schedule leaves the page accurate about the product and wrong about whether it can be bought; each fact needs its own owner, clock and path to every channel.

The reader chose commerce-promotions for (a), citing how offers combine and how discounts reach invoices and refunds, and commerce-search-and-discovery for (b), citing the index as a maintained copy and the missing attributes and synonyms. Both match the expected answer.
